fields.sections.3.exchanges.1.con.words: Bowen argues that Deuteronomy 20 makes forced labor the best outcome for distant peoples and annihilation the alternative, undermining benign readings of Gibeonite protection.
fields.sections.3.exchanges.1.con.critique: Strongest feature: Bowen answers the protective reading of the Gibeonite episode by connecting it to Deuteronomy 20’s coercive alternatives: distant peoples submit to compulsory tribute labor, while people under the ban face annihilation. Principal limitation: He identifies Deuteronomy 20, the distant-versus-local distinction, and the Gibeonite outcome, but the excerpt neither quotes the provisions nor completes their textual demonstration; repetition and specialist terminology also reduce clarity. Live burden: The argument must make those textual anchors explicit enough to establish compulsory labor as the favorable narrative alternative while preserving Bowen’s qualification that corvee labor is not slavery proper under his earlier definition. Locked score: The fixed 83 recognizes a coherent, responsive contextual rebuttal whose specificity and charitable calibration challenge a benign account, with measured deductions for incomplete textual presentation and diminished precision.
